    1. isTerminal()

Interface NextResult<T>

Type Parameters:
T - the type of values carried by NextResult.Value results
All Known Implementing Classes:
NextResult.Cancelled, NextResult.Completed, NextResult.Deleted, NextResult.Errored, NextResult.Expired, NextResult.Timeout, NextResult.Value
public sealed interface NextResult<T> permits NextResult.Value<T>, NextResult.Timeout<T>, NextResult.Completed<T>, NextResult.Expired<T>, NextResult.Deleted<T>, NextResult.Errored<T>, NextResult.Cancelled<T>
Sealed outcome type returned by BlockingSubscription.next(java.time.Duration). Each call to next() returns exactly one of seven variants:
  • NextResult.Value — a new value from the underlying primitive (non-terminal).
  • NextResult.Timeout — the timeout elapsed with no value available (non-terminal).
  • NextResult.Completed — the primitive completed naturally (terminal).
  • NextResult.Expired — the primitive's TTL elapsed without renewal (terminal).
  • NextResult.Deleted — the primitive was explicitly deleted (terminal).
  • NextResult.Errored — an unexpected backend error occurred (terminal).
  • NextResult.Cancelled — this subscription was torn down locally; the underlying primitive may still be alive and reachable by other subscribers (terminal).

Callers should use pattern matching (switch expressions or instanceof checks) to handle each variant. The isTerminal() method provides a quick check: terminal results indicate that no further values will arrive on this subscription.

  • Method Details

    • isTerminal

      default boolean isTerminal()
      Returns true if this result represents the end of the subscription — no more values will arrive. NextResult.Completed, NextResult.Expired, NextResult.Deleted, NextResult.Errored, and NextResult.Cancelled are terminal. NextResult.Value and NextResult.Timeout are not — more values may still arrive on subsequent pulls.
      Returns:
      true if this result is a terminal outcome, false otherwise
